chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The close relative mourns for his close relative for three days, and the wife for her husband for four months and ten days. The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And if a man divorces his wife while he is absent from her, and then the news reaches her of that, and she has menstruated three times from the day he divorced her until that day, then she has completed her waiting period (iddah) and there is no waiting period upon her after that. And if she had menstred less than three times, she should count them as part of the waiting period and build upon them to complete it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman whose husband divorced her while absent and she has experienced three menstrual cycles?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the mourning waiting period (iddah al-wa'ad) as three days for general kin, contrasting it with the four months and ten days prescribed for widows, while also addressing the iddah for divorce. The accompanying commentary by Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the mechanics of completing the iddah in cases of deferred divorce, emphasizing that three menstrual cycles serve as the definitive measure for the woman's release from marital bonds. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential reliance on menstrual cycles as the primary indicator of time passage in personal status law.
